timestampConverter.metaTitle: Unix Timestamp and Epoch Converter to Date
timestampConverter.metaDescription: Convert Unix timestamp and epoch to human-readable date and time. Supports seconds, milliseconds, and datetime to epoch. Shows ISO 8601, UTC, local time, and relative time.
timestampConverter.title: Unix Timestamp / Epoch Converter
timestampConverter.description: Convert Unix timestamp or epoch to date and time, and datetime to epoch. Supports seconds and milliseconds — format is detected automatically.
timestampConverter.inputHint: Accepts Unix timestamps (seconds or milliseconds) or date strings (ISO 8601, YYYY-MM-DD, etc.)
timestampConverter.aboutText: A Unix timestamp (also called Epoch time) is the number of seconds elapsed since January 1, 1970 00:00:00 UTC. It is widely used in APIs, databases, and log files.
timestampConverter.inputError: Invalid timestamp or date. Enter a Unix timestamp (e.g. 1700000000) or a date (e.g. 2024-01-15).
timestampConverter.aboutText: A Unix timestamp — also called Epoch time — is the number of seconds elapsed since January 1, 1970 at 00:00:00 UTC (the "Unix Epoch"). It is the universal time standard in computing: REST APIs, databases, log files, JWT tokens, and messaging systems all use this format because it is simple, compact, and timezone-independent.
timestampConverter.secondsVsMillisText: There are two common formats: epoch in seconds (e.g. 1700000000, 10 digits) and epoch in milliseconds (e.g. 1700000000000, 13 digits). Java uses milliseconds by default — System.currentTimeMillis() returns a long with 13 digits. JavaScript's Date.now() also returns milliseconds. This tool automatically detects the format based on the number of digits.
timestampConverter.codeIntro: Conversion examples between epoch and date in common languages and databases:
timestampConverter.useCaseApi: API responses — fields like created_at, updated_at, and expires_in are commonly epoch in seconds or milliseconds.
timestampConverter.useCaseJwt: JWT tokens — the exp (expiration), iat (issued at), and nbf (not before) fields are epoch in seconds.
timestampConverter.useCaseLog: Log files — epoch timestamps allow efficient sorting and filtering without timezone conversion.
timestampConverter.useCaseDb: Databases — BIGINT columns storing epoch in milliseconds are common in high-performance systems.
timestampConverter.useCaseScheduler: Schedulers and queues — systems like Celery, BullMQ, and cron jobs use epoch to calculate future execution times.
timestampConverter.howToUse: Type or paste a Unix timestamp (seconds or milliseconds) to see all date and time representations. Or paste a date in any format — ISO 8601, UTC, local date — to get the corresponding epoch. Click Use Now to load the current timestamp. Every result has an individual copy button.
timestampConverter.privacyNote: All conversions are calculated locally in your browser. No data is sent to any server.
timestampConverter.codePython:
import time
from datetime import datetime, timezone

# Current epoch (seconds)
now = int(time.time())

# Epoch → datetime
dt = datetime.fromtimestamp(1700000000, tz=timezone.utc)
print(dt.isoformat())  # 2023-11-14T22:13:20+00:00

# datetime → Epoch
epoch = int(datetime(2024, 1, 15, 10, 30, tzinfo=timezone.utc).timestamp())
timestampConverter.codeSQL:
-- MySQL / PostgreSQL
SELECT FROM_UNIXTIME(1700000000);               -- epoch → datetime
SELECT UNIX_TIMESTAMP(''2024-01-15 10:30:00''); -- datetime → epoch

-- SQL Server
SELECT DATEADD(SECOND, 1700000000, ''1970-01-01'');
timestampConverter.faq1Q: How do I convert a Unix timestamp to a readable date?
timestampConverter.faq1A: Paste the timestamp (in seconds or milliseconds) into the field above. The tool automatically detects the format and shows ISO 8601, UTC, local time, date only, and relative time — each with a copy button.
timestampConverter.faq2Q: What is the difference between epoch in seconds and milliseconds?
timestampConverter.faq2A: Epoch in seconds has 10 digits (e.g. 1700000000). Epoch in milliseconds has 13 digits (e.g. 1700000000000). Java uses milliseconds in System.currentTimeMillis(). POSIX and Unix APIs use seconds. This tool detects the format automatically based on digit count.
timestampConverter.faq3Q: How do I convert a Java long to a date?
timestampConverter.faq3A: A Java long from System.currentTimeMillis() represents milliseconds since the Epoch. Paste the value into the tool — it detects the 13 digits and converts automatically. In code: Instant.ofEpochMilli(longValue) or new Date(longValue) on the front end.
timestampConverter.faq4Q: How do I convert a date to Unix timestamp (datetime to epoch)?
timestampConverter.faq4A: Paste the date in any supported format — ISO 8601 like 2024-01-15T10:30:00Z, or simply 2024-01-15 — and the tool returns the epoch in seconds and milliseconds ready to copy.
timestampConverter.faq5Q: Is the exp field in a JWT in seconds or milliseconds?
timestampConverter.faq5A: Always seconds, as specified by RFC 7519. The exp, iat, and nbf fields in JWT tokens use Unix timestamps in seconds. If you paste an exp value and the result shows an absurd year (50000+), the value is likely in milliseconds — divide by 1000 first.

cpfCnpj.metaTitle: CNPJ Generator for Developers and Testing
cpfCnpj.metaDescription: Generate valid CNPJ numbers for software development and testing in one click. Supports the new alphanumeric CNPJ format and CPF. Free tool for developers and QA teams.
cpfCnpj.title: CNPJ Generator and Validator Online
cpfCnpj.description: Generate CNPJ for development, software testing, and QA. Supports numeric CNPJ, alphanumeric CNPJ (new format since 2026), and CPF — all with correct check digits.
cpfCnpj.warning: These numbers are fictitious and generated for software testing and development purposes only. Any other use is illegal.
cpfCnpj.placeholder: Enter a CPF or CNPJ (with or without formatting)
cpfCnpj.pasteHint: Paste a CPF or CNPJ below — with or without formatting.
cpfCnpj.testingWarning: The generated numbers are mathematically valid and may coincidentally match real records. Use them exclusively in development, QA, and testing environments.
cpfCnpj.aboutText: This tool generates CPF and CNPJ numbers with correct check digits for use in software testing, QA automation, and development. It supports numeric CNPJ, the new alphanumeric CNPJ format (IN RFB nº 2.229/2024), and CPF.
cpfCnpj.algorithmText: CPF and CNPJ use a weighted modulo-11 algorithm. Each digit is multiplied by a decreasing weight, the sum is divided by 11, and the remainder determines the check digits. The alphanumeric CNPJ uses the same algorithm — letters are encoded as their ASCII code minus 48 (so A = 17, B = 18, …, Z = 42).
cpfCnpj.howToUse: Select the document type and quantity, then click Generate. Use the Validate tab to check whether an existing CPF or CNPJ is mathematically valid. Copy the formatted or raw value with one click. Export multiple generated documents as JSON or CSV for test fixtures or database seeds.
cpfCnpj.privacyNote: All documents are generated and validated locally in your browser. No CPF or CNPJ values are ever sent to any server or analytics.
cpfCnpj.faq1Q: How do I generate a valid CNPJ for testing?
cpfCnpj.faq1A: Use the tool above: select the type (numeric or alphanumeric CNPJ), choose the quantity, and click Generate. The numbers have mathematically correct check digits and are accepted by any CNPJ validator.
cpfCnpj.faq2Q: Does the generated CNPJ belong to a real company?
cpfCnpj.faq2A: No. CNPJs are generated randomly using the correct algorithm. They may coincidentally match a registration at Receita Federal, but they are created exclusively for software testing — never for real identification or fraudulent purposes.
cpfCnpj.faq3Q: What is the alphanumeric CNPJ and why does my system need to support it?
cpfCnpj.faq3A: Since July 31, 2026, Receita Federal issues CNPJs with letters (A–Z) in the 12 base positions. Systems that handle CNPJ must update validations, input masks, regex patterns, and database columns to support the new format.
cpfCnpj.faq4Q: How do I validate an existing CNPJ with this tool?
cpfCnpj.faq4A: Use the Validate tab above. Paste a CPF or CNPJ with or without formatting — the result appears immediately, showing whether it is valid and the detected type (CPF, numeric CNPJ, or alphanumeric CNPJ).
cpfCnpj.faq5Q: Can I export multiple CNPJs at once for test fixtures?
cpfCnpj.faq5A: Yes. Generate the desired quantity and click Export JSON or Export CSV. The downloaded file is ready to use in automated test fixtures or database seeds.

cnpjAlpha.metaTitle: Alphanumeric CNPJ — What Changed and How It Works
cnpjAlpha.metaDescription: Receita Federal issued the first alphanumeric CNPJ (00.000.000/E08G-12) on July 31, 2026. Learn the new algorithm, validation rules, and how to update your systems.
cnpjAlpha.title: Alphanumeric CNPJ
cnpjAlpha.subtitle: What changed on July 31, 2026 — and what your system needs to handle
cnpjAlpha.backgroundText: On July 31, 2026, the Receita Federal do Brasil issued the first alphanumeric CNPJ: 00.000.000/E08G-12. This change is governed by IN RFB nº 2.229, published in 2024, which expanded the CNPJ format to support letters in any of the 12 base positions.
cnpjAlpha.whyText: The numeric CNPJ namespace was approaching exhaustion. By allowing alphanumeric characters (A–Z, 0–9) across all 12 base positions, the Receita Federal expanded the available registration space by many orders of magnitude. Both old numeric CNPJs and new alphanumeric ones coexist permanently.
cnpjAlpha.structureRootDesc: Identifies the legal entity. Can be numeric (legacy) or alphanumeric (new registrations).
cnpjAlpha.structureBranchDesc: Identifies the establishment. Can be numeric or alphanumeric. Official example: 12.ABC.345/01DE-35.
cnpjAlpha.structureCheckDesc: Always two numeric digits. Calculated using the same algorithm for both formats.
cnpjAlpha.algorithmText: The check digits use the same formula for both numeric and alphanumeric CNPJs. Each character is converted to a numeric value using charCode - 48 (not standard base-36):
cnpjAlpha.algorithmWeights: Weights for D1: [5,4,3,2,9,8,7,6,5,4,3,2] applied to positions 1–12. Weights for D2: [6,5,4,3,2,9,8,7,6,5,4,3,2] applied to positions 1–13 (including D1).
cnpjAlpha.algorithmRemainder: Result = remainder % 11. If remainder < 2, digit = 0. Otherwise digit = 11 - remainder.
cnpjAlpha.exampleText: First alphanumeric CNPJ issued (Banco do Brasil branch, July 31, 2026): 00.000.000/E08G-12. Verification:
cnpjAlpha.exampleOfficialFull: Official example with letters in both root and branch: 12.ABC.345/01DE-35.
cnpjAlpha.systemsTitle: What to Update in Your Systems
cnpjAlpha.systemsMask: Input masks: update patterns to accept A–Z in all 14 positions except the last two (check digits).
cnpjAlpha.systemsRegex: Validation regex: replace \d with [0-9A-Z] for the first 12 characters; keep \d for the 2 check digits.
cnpjAlpha.systemsDb: Database columns: CNPJ fields must be VARCHAR(18) (not INT/BIGINT). Store as text to preserve leading zeros and letters.
cnpjAlpha.systemsCase: Case handling: normalize to uppercase before validation. Store uppercase. Lowercase input is valid and should be accepted.
cnpjAlpha.toolText: Use the CPF/CNPJ tool to validate both numeric and alphanumeric CNPJs.
